name: second-theme-pick-repaints-the-sidebar
description:
proves the second-pick signature the diagnosis predicts, then covers three more checks in the same VM pass. AppearanceValuesDiffer used to compare the accent's space flag but never overlay_theme, so DetermineSettingsApplyChanges saw no difference between two named themes and skipped SetWindowAppearance. Fixing that gate exposed a second, deeper gap: ApplyWindowAppearance's accent-handling block assigned the new theme and called nothing, so PushOverlayTheme's nine-surface fan-out only ever ran from each surface's own one-shot ready handshake, never from a live edit - the gate fix alone left the symptom 100 percent present. Both are fixed: AppearanceValuesDiffer is now a defaulted WindowAppearance::operator==, and ApplyWindowAppearance calls PushAiPanelInk() at the end of its accent-handling block.

The gate: covered by the C++ unit test, AtriumSettingsApplyChangesTest.AThemeOnlyChangeStillFiresAppearance.
Every surface (not just the one that repaints): reads the command bar's tokens across the SAME two picks the sidebar is read across, not a fresh pick - opened once before either pick and never reopened, so CommandBarWidget::Show's own re-push on open cannot be mistaken for the live fan-out.
Survives a restart: relaunch (Cmd+Q, then Atrium again against the same staged settings.json, no restaging) and re-read the sidebar.

The settings window hosts the picker but was not one of PushAiPanelInk's nine surfaces, so it kept the brand default through both picks. settings-tokens/accent-after-{first,second}-pick read the settings document the same way the command bar is read, and the eval_changed between them is the deciding assertion for that gap.
